task.title: Page materialized recurrence occurrence bindings
task.objective: Complete issue https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/899 by inspecting complete materialized task bindings through one allocation-bounded exact-recurrence authored window.
acceptance_criteria: Inspect at most the validated page-size bound and return bindings in ascending authored-offset order.
Advance the cursor by inspected authored coordinates across missing and persisted-only gaps.
Fail closed on selected-window corruption while isolating unrelated and out-of-window evidence.

attempts.patch: Added focused integration coverage for the acceptance contract before adding production behavior.

attempts.patch: Added bounded authored-window paging over canonical strict occurrence replay and returned only complete materialized projections.

attempts.diagnostic: Independent review and the substantive automated walkthrough found no actionable defect; the exact one-commit head passed the Rust quality gate.
attempts.patch: Reused definition paging, occurrence-state validation, and the shared page-size/error contracts. Reran the complete repository quality gate after the exact implementation state was ready.

outcome.summary: The kernel pages sparse materialized recurrence bindings deterministically without treating gaps as cursor termination or broadening lifecycle authority.

verification.command: nix develop --command cargo run --locked -p vela-dev -- record validate corpus/development/0180-materialized-recurrence-paging.json # result: valid development record
nix develop --command cargo run --locked -p vela-dev -- corpus inspect corpus/development # result: inspected 185 records: 185 valid, 0 invalid

lessons: Sparse result density must not control cursor progress; authored coordinates are the stable paging domain.
Selected-window corruption should fail the page before partial output, while unrelated evidence remains outside the query boundary.
Reusing exact occurrence replay keeps paging provenance aligned with single-coordinate lookup.
Materialized inspection is read-only and grants no due selection, catch-up, dispatch, retry, or execution authority.
